# Report information

Focused **peptide-chemistry** report for immunopeptidomics experiments. Where
the other reports describe *which* peptides were found, this one describes
*what they are made of*: amino-acid composition, per-position residue
preferences, and per-peptide physicochemical descriptors (GRAVY, pI, net
charge, ...), compared between Conditions. The
methods and the reasoning behind them are documented in the *Methods &
justification* section at the end.

`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "setup.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo")}
```


```{r pepchem-prep, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------
pepchem_input <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") pep_all else pep_short
peptide_set_label <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") "all peptides" else
  paste0("selected peptides (", shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs)")

# Descriptors are sequence-intrinsic: computed once over the unique sequences,
# then attached to each (Sample, Sequence) pair.
props <- pepchem_by_sample(pepchem_input, ph = params$ChargePh)
glossary_pepchem <- TRUE # the shared glossary adds the descriptor table
property_cols <- pepchem_properties(params$PropertySet)
property_cols <- intersect(property_cols, names(props))

# ---- per-sample summaries and their Condition aggregation -------------------
pepchem_summary <- summarise_pepchem(props, by = "Sample",
                                     properties = property_cols)
pepchem_condition <- aggregate_pepchem(pepchem_summary, stat = "Median")

n_seq_sample <- props |>
  dplyr::count(Sample, Condition, name = "n_Sequences") |>
  dplyr::mutate(Flag = ifelse(n_Sequences < params$MinPeptidesSample,
                              "below MinPeptidesSample", ""))
low_samples <- as.character(n_seq_sample$Sample[nzchar(n_seq_sample$Flag)])
if (length(low_samples) > 0)
  warning(length(low_samples), " sample(s) carry fewer than ",
          params$MinPeptidesSample, " unique sequences and their summaries are ",
          "noisy: ", paste(low_samples, collapse = ", "))

# ---- composition ------------------------------------------------------------
aa_by_condition <- aa_composition(props$Sequence, groups = props$Condition)
aa_by_sample    <- aa_composition(props$Sequence, groups = props$Sample)

# ---- per-position frequency -------------------------------------------------
motif_length <- if (identical(tolower(as.character(params$MotifLength)), "auto"))
  NULL else suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$MotifLength))
if (!is.null(motif_length) && is.na(motif_length)) {
  warning("MotifLength = '", params$MotifLength,
          "' is not \"auto\" nor an integer; falling back to the modal length.")
  motif_length <- NULL
}
aa_positions <- aa_position_frequency(props$Sequence, length = motif_length,
                                      groups = props$Condition)
motif_length_used <- attr(aa_positions, "length")

terminal_positions <- suppressWarnings(
  as.integer(trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$TerminalPositions), ",")[[1]])))
terminal_positions <- terminal_positions[!is.na(terminal_positions)]
aa_terminal <- if (length(terminal_positions) == 0) aa_positions[0, ] else
  aa_position_frequency(props$Sequence, length = NULL,
                        positions = terminal_positions, groups = props$Condition)

# ---- statistics -------------------------------------------------------------
can_compare <- n_conditions >= 2
pepchem_stats <- pepchem_stats_peptide <- aa_stats <- NULL
if (can_compare) {
  pepchem_stats <- compare_pepchem(props, level = "sample",
                                   properties = property_cols,
                                   fdr = params$FdrCutoff)
  pepchem_stats_peptide <- compare_pepchem(props, level = "peptide",
                                           properties = property_cols,
                                           fdr = params$FdrCutoff)
  aa_stats <- compare_aa_frequency(props, fdr = params$FdrCutoff)
} else {
  warning("Only one Condition in this subset - no between-condition comparison ",
          "is possible; the descriptive sections are still rendered.")
}
```

**Peptide set:** `r peptide_set_label` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **descriptors:**
`r params$PropertySet` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **unique sequences:**
`r format(dplyr::n_distinct(props$Sequence), big.mark = ",")` &nbsp;|&nbsp;
**charge pH:** `r params$ChargePh` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **FDR:** `r params$FdrCutoff`

# Peptide set overview

Every descriptor below is computed on the **unique sequences of each sample**: a
peptide identified in five replicates contributes one value to each of those
five samples, not five values to its Condition. A sample with very few sequences
gives a noisy median, so the ones below `MinPeptidesSample`
(`r params$MinPeptidesSample`) are flagged here and should be read with care in
the per-sample sections.

```{r overview-table, echo=FALSE}
n_seq_sample |>
  kable(caption = "Unique sequences per sample") |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# Amino acid composition {.tabset}

Position-independent residue frequency. Non-standard residues (`X`, `B`, `Z`,
`U`) are dropped, so the 20 standard residues sum to 1 within each group.

## By Condition

```{r plot-aa-composition-condition, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE}
p_aa_composition_condition <- plot_aa_composition(aa_by_condition, type = "bar")
if (is.null(p_aa_composition_condition))
  cat("_No usable sequence in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_aa_composition_condition, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## By Sample

```{r plot-aa-composition-sample, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}
p_aa_composition_sample <- plot_aa_composition(aa_by_sample, type = "heatmap")
if (is.null(p_aa_composition_sample))
  cat("_No usable sequence in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_aa_composition_sample, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## Enrichment

Log2 of each Condition's residue frequency over the **pooled** frequency of this
subset. The pooled composition is an internal reference, not a proteome
background: it answers "which residues distinguish this Condition from the rest
of this experiment", not "which residues are enriched relative to the source
proteome".

```{r plot-aa-composition-enrichment, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, warning=FALSE}
p_aa_composition_enrichment <- plot_aa_composition(aa_by_condition,
                                                   type = "enrichment")
if (is.null(p_aa_composition_enrichment))
  cat("_No usable sequence in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_aa_composition_enrichment, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## Statistics

Per-residue comparison of the **per-sample** frequencies (see *Methods*).

```{r aa-stats-table, echo=FALSE}
if (is.null(aa_stats) || nrow(aa_stats) == 0) {
  cat("_Fewer than two Conditions in this subset - no comparison possible._")
} else {
  aa_stats |>
    dplyr::select(AA, Contrast, Median1, Median2, Log2Ratio, CliffsDelta,
                  p_value, p_adj, Significant) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                function(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
}
```

# Positional amino acid frequency {.tabset}

Residue frequency at each aligned position. This is the numeric complement to
the sequence logos in the `01_mhc_overview` report: a logo scales its letters by
information content, so a position with a mild but consistent preference almost
disappears, while the heatmap keeps every frequency readable and directly
comparable between Conditions.

## Dominant length

```{r plot-aa-position, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}
p_aa_position <- plot_aa_position_heatmap(aa_positions, ncol = phis_ncol)
if (is.null(p_aa_position))
  cat("_Not enough equal-length peptides for a positional profile._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_aa_position, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

`r if (!is.null(motif_length_used)) paste0("Computed on the ", motif_length_used, "-mers of this subset.") else ""`

## Terminal positions (all lengths)

Positions `r params$TerminalPositions` resolved against each peptide's own
length (negative values count from the C-terminus), so peptides of every length
contribute. This is where an HLA-I anchor shift shows up even when the length
distribution itself is unchanged.

```{r plot-aa-terminal, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}
p_aa_terminal <- plot_aa_position_heatmap(
  aa_terminal, ncol = phis_ncol,
  title = "Terminal-position amino-acid frequency (all lengths)")
if (is.null(p_aa_terminal))
  cat("_No usable position in this subset._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_aa_terminal, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

# Physicochemical descriptors {.tabset}

One tab per descriptor. Each shows the **per-peptide** distribution (every unique
sequence of a Condition contributes one value, so the spread is between-peptide)
next to the **per-sample** summary (mean +/- sd across samples of the per-sample
median, so the error bar is replicate reproducibility). The two answer different
questions and are meant to be read together.

```{r plot-properties, results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
property_plots <- list()
for (prop in property_cols) {
  cat("\n\n## ", prop, " {.tabset}\n\n")
  p_dist <- plot_property_distribution(props, prop, type = "density")
  p_summ <- plot_property_sample_summary(pepchem_condition, prop,
                                         points = pepchem_summary)
  if (is.null(p_dist) && is.null(p_summ)) {
    cat("_No usable value for this descriptor._\n\n")
    next
  }
  cat("\n\n### Distribution\n\n")
  if (is.null(p_dist)) cat("_Not available._\n\n") else print(p_dist)
  cat("\n\n### Mean +/- sd (per sample)\n\n")
  if (is.null(p_summ)) cat("_Not available._\n\n") else print(p_summ)
  property_plots[[prop]] <- list(distribution = p_dist, summary = p_summ)
}
```

# Between-condition comparison

```{r plot-effectsize, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}
p_effectsize <- plot_property_effectsize(pepchem_stats, fdr = params$FdrCutoff)
if (is.null(p_effectsize))
  cat("_Fewer than two Conditions in this subset - no comparison possible._") else
  ggprint_rawr(p_effectsize, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## Sample level (primary)

Each sample contributes one value per descriptor (its median over that sample's
unique sequences), and Conditions are compared across samples. Samples are the
real replicates, so this is the honest test — and it is deliberately
low-powered: with three replicates per Condition a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum
test **cannot** return a p-value below 0.1, whatever the effect. Read
`CliffsDelta` and `MedianDiff` first, and treat the p-values as a ranking aid.

```{r pepchem-stats-table, echo=FALSE}
if (is.null(pepchem_stats) || nrow(pepchem_stats) == 0) {
  cat("_Fewer than two Conditions in this subset - no comparison possible._")
} else {
  pepchem_stats |>
    dplyr::select(Property, Contrast, n1, n2, Median1, Median2, MedianDiff,
                  CliffsDelta, p_value, p_adj, Significant) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                function(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
}
```

## Peptide level (descriptive)

The same descriptors pooled over the unique sequences of each Condition. Peptides
from one sample are not independent observations, so these p-values are
anti-conservative by construction and are **not** inference: this track is here
because its effect sizes describe how far the two repertoires actually sit apart,
which the low-powered sample-level test cannot resolve.

```{r pepchem-stats-peptide-table, echo=FALSE}
if (is.null(pepchem_stats_peptide) || nrow(pepchem_stats_peptide) == 0) {
  cat("_Fewer than two Conditions in this subset - no comparison possible._")
} else {
  pepchem_stats_peptide |>
    dplyr::select(Property, Contrast, n1, n2, Median1, Median2, MedianDiff,
                  CliffsDelta, p_value, p_adj, Significant) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                function(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
    DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
}
```

## Overall test per descriptor

Kruskal-Wallis across **all** Conditions at the sample level, before the pairwise
breakdown above.

```{r pepchem-kruskal-table, echo=FALSE}
kw <- if (is.null(pepchem_stats)) NULL else attr(pepchem_stats, "kruskal")
if (is.null(kw) || nrow(kw) == 0) {
  cat("_Fewer than two Conditions in this subset - no comparison possible._")
} else {
  kw |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                function(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
    kable(caption = "Kruskal-Wallis test per descriptor (sample level)") |>
    kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

# Methods & justification

**What is computed.** Every descriptor is a property of the peptide *sequence*,
so it is computed once per unique sequence and then attached to each sample that
identified it. `GRAVY` is the grand average of hydropathy, the mean
Kyte-Doolittle value over the residues (Kyte & Doolittle 1982) and the standard
hydrophobicity summary for a peptide. `pI`, net `Charge` (at pH
`r params$ChargePh`), `MW`, the `Boman` potential-interaction index, the
`HydrophobicMoment`, the `InstabilityIndex` and the `AliphaticIndex` come from
the corresponding functions of the `Peptides` package. The `frac_*` descriptors
are the fraction of residues in each amino-acid class.

**Why the unit of analysis is the sample.** Peptides identified within one
Condition are not independent observations: they come from the same few
pulldowns, share alleles and source proteins, and their number depends on run
depth. Pooling them and testing across peptides gives enormous nominal
significance for effects that may be carried by a single sample. The primary
comparison therefore summarises each **sample** first (median descriptor over its
unique sequences; residue frequency within that sample) and tests across samples,
where the replication is real.

**Why both tracks are shown.** The honest test is also weak. A two-sided Wilcoxon
rank-sum test on 3 vs 3 samples has a minimum attainable p-value of 0.1, so a
perfectly separated descriptor cannot reach a 0.05 FDR — the same structural
limit the `05_quant_stats` report documents for its Fisher presence/absence
track. The peptide-level track is reported alongside, explicitly labelled
descriptive, so the *size* of a difference stays visible when its p-value cannot
clear the cut-off.

**Tests and effect sizes.** Kruskal-Wallis across all Conditions, then a pairwise
Wilcoxon rank-sum test per Condition pair, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected within
each contrast (the family is "all descriptors, or all 20 residues, tested for
this pair"). Non-parametric tests are used because several descriptors are
bounded or strongly skewed (`Charge`, the `frac_*` fractions) and no
distributional assumption is safe across them. Two effect sizes accompany every
test: `MedianDiff`, on the descriptor's own scale, and `CliffsDelta`, which is
scale-free and therefore comparable between descriptors measured in different
units.

**Amino-acid frequencies** are tested the same way, on per-sample frequencies. A
chi-square test on pooled residue counts was deliberately not used: it would
treat every residue of every peptide as an independent draw and return
vanishingly small p-values for differences well inside the between-sample
spread.

**Limitations.** The composition enrichment tab compares each Condition against
the pooled composition of this subset, not against the source proteome — a
proteome background needs the search FASTA, which this report does not read.
Peptide position within the parent protein is likewise out of scope. Descriptors
are computed on the unmodified `Sequence`, so post-translational modifications do
not shift the reported mass, charge or hydrophobicity; see the PTM profile in
`01_mhc_overview` for those.

Kyte J & Doolittle RF (1982) *J Mol Biol* 157:105. Osorio D, Rondon-Villarreal P
& Torres R (2015) *R Journal* 7:4 (the `Peptides` package). Boman HG (2003)
*J Intern Med* 254:197. Cliff N (1993) *Psychol Bull* 114:494. Benjamini Y &
Hochberg Y (1995) *J R Stat Soc B* 57:289.

```{r export-results, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Always-written exports: render parameters + the per-sample summary and stats
write_input_params(params, folder = FolderResults,
                   prefix = paste(c(result_prefix, "04_pepchem"), collapse = "_"))
write.csv_rawr(pepchem_summary, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
if (!is.null(pepchem_stats))
  write.csv_rawr(pepchem_stats, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)

if (params$CsvSave) {
  aa_composition_condition <- aa_by_condition
  aa_composition_sample    <- aa_by_sample
  aa_position_table        <- aa_positions
  aa_terminal_table        <- aa_terminal
  pepchem_condition_summary <- pepchem_condition
  write.csv_rawr(aa_composition_condition, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(aa_composition_sample, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(aa_position_table, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(aa_terminal_table, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(pepchem_condition_summary, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  if (!is.null(pepchem_stats_peptide)) {
    pepchem_stats_peptide_level <- pepchem_stats_peptide
    write.csv_rawr(pepchem_stats_peptide_level, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  }
  if (!is.null(aa_stats)) {
    aa_frequency_stats <- aa_stats
    write.csv_rawr(aa_frequency_stats, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  }
}

if (params$PlotsSave) {
  static_plots <- list(p_aa_composition_condition = p_aa_composition_condition,
                       p_aa_composition_sample = p_aa_composition_sample,
                       p_aa_composition_enrichment = p_aa_composition_enrichment,
                       p_aa_position = p_aa_position,
                       p_aa_terminal = p_aa_terminal,
                       p_effectsize = p_effectsize)
  for (nm in names(static_plots)) {
    if (!is.null(static_plots[[nm]]))
      ggsave_rawr(static_plots[[nm]], file = nm, folder = FolderFigures,
                  width = 20, height = 14)
  }
  for (prop in names(property_plots)) {
    if (!is.null(property_plots[[prop]]$distribution))
      ggsave_rawr(property_plots[[prop]]$distribution,
                  file = paste0("p_dist_", prop), folder = FolderFigures,
                  width = 18, height = 12)
    if (!is.null(property_plots[[prop]]$summary))
      ggsave_rawr(property_plots[[prop]]$summary,
                  file = paste0("p_sample_", prop), folder = FolderFigures,
                  width = 18, height = 12)
  }
}
```
